newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bank merger not discussed for months -SGB.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bank merger not discussed for months -SGB.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) said on Wednesday there had been no contacts between its Generale Bank and BBL about the creation of a big Belgian bank since around May 1996.

SGB supported the idea of the creation of a big Belgian bank but for now the project "is the freezer. Since May or June 1996 there have been no contacts between the shareholders or the boards of Generale Bank and BBL," SGB chairman Etienne Davignon told a news conference.
"Therefore all the talk of the imminence of the creation of a large Belgian bank is a surprise to me," he said.

If a big Belgian bank merger occurred there should be no conflicts of interest between the new institution's shareholders. "At this moment...I do not see any possibility of this condition being fulfilled," he said.
SGB is Generale Bank's largest shareholder.

Dutch bancassurance group ING last year blocked a merger betwen the bank and BBL -- Banque Bruxelles Lambert -- because it insisted on holding a 20 percent stake in the new merged group, matching its current stake in BBL.
BBL's largest shareholder is Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
